### 4a. Exact performance scope and unavailable historical benchmark

The hot-path requirement is scoped by **both the consumer and the optional event snapshot**. Independent inspection of the frozen `trigger_suppression.rs::death_suppressed_before` and `death_suppressed_after` (lines 160–174) finds a lazy `map_or_else`: Some(snapshot), including Some(empty), reads the selected vector and never invokes the missing-history closure. None invokes `active_suppress_trigger_statics(state)` **on each helper call**. A board with zero suppressors still requires that enumeration to discover the empty list. Therefore a None event matching multiple candidates/clauses can repeatedly scan the battlefield. This is an acknowledged cost of the bounded legacy/unavailable-history compatibility path, not an optimized path established by v9.

Ordinary `collect_pending_triggers` builds one live suppression list per nonempty collection pass. Its event-wide ETB gate and batched ETB prefilter borrow that list. Excluded ordinary NotEquals/OneOf clauses also borrow it through `match_for_ordinary_collection`; registered delayed ambiguous clauses remain ungated by their None **consumer context**, which is distinct from record.snapshot None. Repaired unambiguous ordinary/delayed clauses plus Haunt and death-caused Unattach use the snapshot helpers; with record None these can rescan even when an ordinary cache already exists. A source inspection of Some cannot prove the performance of None, and a live cache elsewhere cannot be described as being passed to these helpers when it is not.

V10 retains the current fallback implementation. No new ABI/context, persistent cache, global/static state, layer invalidation protocol or suppression semantics change is justified solely by this unmeasured qualification. Reusing the ordinary cache for every dedicated/registered consumer would require additional context plumbing and independent correctness proof; it is not implicit work under this plan. The none-record behavior is permitted for legacy/synthetic/unavailable nested records only within the previously declared timing limits. New in-scope actual departures must still be Some, and a missing new snapshot is an implementation failure, not a performance or compatibility excuse.

Required evidence and report:

- Keep the structural gate on the repaired hot paths: inspect both helper branches, every call site, owner before/after capture, ordinary and batched ETB and ambiguous adapters. Some(empty) must remain authoritative without a live scan; one capture boundary evaluates each candidate once in each selected world using its shared active list, with no added per-member flush. Keep the existing fresh Some(empty)-then-later-Hush and captured-Dies-after-source-left runtime/serde controls and every source-capture mutation. Audit actual emitted records in the new public SBA fixtures and all prior acceptance rows so a silently unavailable record cannot satisfy this gate.
- Keep missing-history compatibility tests and explicit labels. Old JSON without snapshot stays None; newly populated empty remains Some. Supplement, if not already covered, with a private `#[cfg(test)]` module in the already authorized `trigger_suppression.rs` file with coherent seeded record/source helper tests for None and Some(empty/Dies), before and after, with and without a functioning live suppressor. Use a coherent Creature departure record: None is suppressed before/after exactly when a functioning live Dies suppressor matches; Some(empty) stays false with that live suppressor, and Some(Dies) stays true after its source is gone. Include asymmetric Some(before=[Dies], after=[]) and its inverse, expecting distinct before/after results. Assert unchanged snapshot payload; private synthetic tests do not claim a reachable historical event. An isolated exact Some-to-live-fallback mutation must fail the existing public/event-history authoritative-empty or retained-Dies guard. No timing threshold or universal scan-count assertion is inferred from these semantic checks.
- Run and record the five existing committed Scute batching guards after any relevant source change. Preserve exact test names/commands and behavioral outcomes, separate from timing. Retain both existing ignored snapshot diagnostics unchanged and the absent-input receipt; execution that returns early for absent input is **unavailable/skipped**, never measured or passed throughput.
- The historical Scute benchmark obligation is explicitly **unavailable, carried as a final performance limitation**, not silently completed and not repaired by constructing an invented `/tmp/gamestate.json`. No production change in v10 is required to make that input exist. If the original snapshot later becomes available, bind its hash and execute the unchanged original/candidate checks on separate targets, identical command/profile and a quiet machine. Otherwise final review/acceptance may proceed only with this availability qualification stated, not a claim of historical performance parity. A separately authorized self-contained benchmark would be a new workload and must be labeled as such; it cannot inherit the historical baseline or prove the entire fallback path.
- If subsequent source changes touch this hot candidate loop, redo the relevant structural/behavioral audit and collect available targeted timing evidence on exactly described workloads; a reproducible regression returns for review. Current evidence establishes no measured throughput regression and no measured throughput improvement. Do not fabricate either conclusion, omit the known None rescan cost, or weaken a runtime correctness assertion to meet a performance narrative.

This is an explicit scope correction to v9's unqualified no-suppressor sentence. The production correctness, ordinary live cache, per-boundary capture, registered-delayed identity, old-save semantics and Some/None distinction are retained. It does not create another rules-support exclusion or permit a fresh candidate record to fall back.
